text.en:
At a level crossing Sana saw two parallel railway tracks and a straight road cutting across them.
"The road makes the same angle with each track," said her father. "That is because the tracks are parallel."

When two lines cross, they form four angles. Angles opposite each other are called vertically opposite angles and they are equal. Two angles side by side on a straight line add up to 180° and are called a linear pair.
Lines that never meet, however far they are extended, are parallel. A line that cuts two or more lines is a transversal. When a transversal cuts two parallel lines, corresponding angles are equal, alternate interior angles are equal, and co-interior angles add up to 180°.
These facts help us find unknown angles. If one angle is 70° then its vertically opposite angle is 70° and the angle next to it on the line is 180° − 70° = 110°.
When two lines cross, vertically opposite angles are equal.
Two angles forming a straight line add up to 180 degrees. This is a linear pair.
A transversal cuts parallel lines. Corresponding angles are equal and alternate interior angles are equal.
Co-interior angles on parallel lines add up to 180 degrees.

problem.en: Two lines cross and one angle is 70°. Find the other three angles.

text.en: The angle next to 70° on a straight line is 180° − 70° = 110°.
The fourth angle is also 110°. So the angles are 70°, 110°, 70°, 110°.

prompt.en: A friend says a linear pair always adds up to 90°. How will you correct this?

requiredIdeas.en: A linear pair lies on a straight line, so it adds up to 180°.

points.en: A linear pair adds up to 180°.
On parallel lines, corresponding and alternate angles are equal.
